newsitem.title: ITALY: Ice chunk falls from glacier in Italian Alps.
newsitem.headline: Ice chunk falls from glacier in Italian Alps.

text.p: A 10,000-15,000 cubic metre chunk of glacier that had been threatening the Italian Alpine ski resort of Courmayeur has finally fallen, but without causing a much-feared avalanche, officials said on Saturday.
"It fell overnight," Courmayeur's mayor Ferdinando Derriard told Reuters. "No-one was hurt, there was no-one in the valley."

Oscar Taiola, head of the town's avalanche committee, said by telephone that the ice mass had broken into bits as it fell from 4,050 metres (13,500 feet) in the Grandes Jorasses peaks close to Mont Blanc, Europe's highest mountain.
All danger was now over, he said.
Derriard declared a state of emergency earlier in the week, barring the Val Ferret valley which had been at risk from a feared massive avalanche as a result of the ice fall.
The nearby hamlet of Planpincieux was evacuated and two hotels, three restaurants and ski hire shops closed.
A cross-country ski piste in the Val Ferret was also shut but the downhill pistes in Courmayeur were not deemed at risk as they are in a different part of the valley.

Taiola said the ice mass, which dropped off "the nose" of a hanging glacier and rolled along the side of the mountain, "exploded" as it fell some 2,000 metres into the Val Ferrat away from populated areas. An avalanche was therefore avoided.
"People are going back home now. It's all fine," he said.
